title: Timestamps are microseconds; extra digits are dropped
description: `TIMESTAMP_LTZ` and `TIMESTAMP_NTZ` hold a 64-bit count of microseconds, from `-290308-12-21 19:59:06.224192` to `+294247-01-10 04:00:54.775807`. Parsing `2024-01-01 00:00:00.123456789` keeps `.123456` and drops the rest, in a cast and in a literal, without an error in either mode. Behind `spark.sql.timestampNanosTypes.enabled`, a preview flag that is off in production and on under Spark's own tests (`Utils.isTesting`), Spark 4.3.0 also has `TIMESTAMP_NTZ(p)` and `TIMESTAMP_LTZ(p)` for p from 7 to 9: a cast to them keeps p digits and floors the rest (`.123456789` as `timestamp_ntz(7)` is `.1234567`). The cast.sql cases rely on that test default; timestamp-ntz-nanos.sql sets the flag.
reference: `precision_timestamp` at 0, 3, 6, 9 (#323); the reference's timestamps are microseconds. Spark is native at 6; nanosecond timestamps lose digits.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(0.1234567d)` is `1969-12-31 16:00:00.123456`: the seventh digit is dropped
`TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(1230219000123123)` raises `DATETIME_OVERFLOW`: past the 64-bit microsecond range, ANSI on
`TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(0.1234567)` (a decimal) raises `java.lang.ArithmeticException: Rounding necessary` with no error class, where a double truncates
`cast(cast('2020-01-01 00:00:00.123456789' as timestamp_ntz(9)) as timestamp_ntz)` is `….123456` (the nanosecond preview types are on under tests)
`typeof(cast('2022-01-01 00:00:00.123456789' as timestamp_ntz(9)))` is `timestamp_ntz(9)`, with the flag at its test default
`.123456789` cast to `timestamp_ntz(7)` and back to string is `.1234567`: floored to 7 digits
with `--SET spark.sql.timestampNanosTypes.enabled=true`, `CAST('2020-01-01 00:00:00.123456789' AS timestamp_ntz(7))` is a `timestamp_ntz(7)` column, `.1234567`

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.

evidence.note: `spark.sql.timestampNanosTypes.enabled` is internal, since 4.3.0, a preview (SPARK-56822), and defaults to `Utils.isTesting`: off in production, on in Spark's tests
